Messages.Author: Joscha
Messages.Body:
Sorry guys, I didn't found an answer in past mails (I only found an
upset discussion about allies playing cards as vampires, but nothing
about Disarm).

So does a Rock Cat counts as a vampire who inflicted more damage at
close range in the combat as the card text of Disarm demands?

I'd say no, because prior to playing the Disarm the Rock Cat did not
count as an vampire inflicting more damage. Only at the time the Cat
plays Disarm it counts as a vampire so the condition for playing Disarm
is not given. But I'm rather unsure.

Disarm, Combat, Potence, R , [Sabbat:R, SW:R, CE:PB, BH:PN]

[pot] Only usable at the end of a round of combat in which this vampire
successfully inflicted more damage at close range than the opposing
vampire. Not usable by a vampire being burned or going into torpor. Put
this card on the opposing vampire and send that vampire into torpor.
The vampire with this card has -1 strength. He or she may burn this
card by burning 3 blood. A vampire can have only one Disarm. [POT] As
above, but the vampire with this card has -2 strength.

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Joscha wrote:
> Sorry guys, I didn't found an answer in past mails (I only found an
> upset discussion about allies playing cards as vampires, but nothing
> about Disarm).
>
> So does a Rock Cat counts as a vampire who inflicted more damage at
> close range in the combat as the card text of Disarm demands?

He is "this vampire" for puposes of playing Disarm, so yes.

If he ("this vampire") inflicted more damage at close range, then
he can play Disarm.
